notes.text: Chris Kreider is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 7 games.
Kaiden Guhle is out (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-four defenseman.
Josh Anderson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 6 games.
Mike Matheson is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-four defenseman.
Dylan Larkin was added to the roster on Nov 24 and has played beside Alexandre Texier and Alex Newhook.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 25 games, up from 6% last season.

Noah Hanifin is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan. That pair has had 68% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 88:42 together, up from 43% with Hanifin.

stakes: The Canadiens go in tied for third in the Atlantic with 32 points, the Golden Knights second in the Pacific with 35 points.

VGK.head: The Golden Knights start a half-step ahead
VGK.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, but they are on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Hanifin. Still, it’s close: the Canadiens can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

MTL.head: A slightly uphill night for the Canadiens
MTL.body: Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, but they are on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Hanifin. The Canadiens can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: A good test for both
paras: The Golden Knights (15-7-5) lost 4-1 to San Jose last night, and the Canadiens are on a three-game losing streak. Two good teams meet. Going in, the Habs are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (sixth).

The Canadiens’ record (.615) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.541), largely because they’re 9-7 in one-goal games. The Golden Knights’ record (.648) is about what their chances are worth.
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 89-79, even though they’ve been outscored 56-55 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 27-16.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). The Golden Knights, by contrast, draw more penalties than they take (1st). They also have one of the league’s best penalty kills (3rd) and create chances on the penalty kill (3rd). The Golden Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage against the Canadiens’ penalty kill (24th), and the Canadiens’ knack for getting shots through meets the Golden Knights’ shot blockers.

Lane Hutson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 26 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 8 A / 20 P in 26 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. Jack Eichel (12 G / 22 A / 34 P in 27 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Mitch Marner (4 G / 26 A / 30 P in 25 GP) is next in line.
Jakub Dobeš (4-4-2 / .868 SV% in 10 GS) has struggled for Montréal so far, but is expected to start. Adin Hill (7-2-3 / .898 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to go for Vegas.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Kaiden Guhle, and have been without Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Mike Matheson for several games.
The Golden Knights have been without Noah Hanifin since Nov 8.
Cole Caufield has scored in three straight games against Vegas.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 8.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
